Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testEncodingInputStream` verifies that the encoding passed to the `ArchiveStreamFactory` is correctly used when creating archive input streams for different archive types. The failure and the given bug report indicate that the encoding is not passed correctly to the constructors of some archive input streams, leading to mismatches in expected encoding.

Examining `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(String archiverName, InputStream in)` reveals that for some archive types (e.g., ArjArchiveInputStream, CpioArchiveInputStream, DumpArchiveInputStream, JarArchiveInputStream), the factory tries to use an internal field `entryEncoding` when constructing the streams. However, the use is inconsistent: for some formats, encoding is always passed, while for others, it may not be passed if `entryEncoding` is null.

The `entryEncoding` field is set during construction of the factory (`ArchiveStreamFactory(String encoding)`), where `entryEncoding` is assigned to the provided encoding value. Also, there is a deprecated setter `setEntryEncoding` that throws if an encoding was set by constructor, which suggests immutability.

The test method `getInputStreamFor` calls `factory.createArchiveInputStream` with a type and an input stream, thus using the `createArchiveInputStream` method examined.

The failure and the bug report summary indicate that certain archive input streams like `ArjArchiveInputStream`, `CpioArchiveInputStream`, `DumpArchiveInputStream`, and `JarArchiveInputStream` do not consistently receive this encoding, causing test failures.

Hence, the root cause is: `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream` does not properly pass the encoding (`entryEncoding`) to all archive input streams it creates. Some constructors are called without the encoding, even though it should be passed, leading to incorrect encoding handling.

This explains why the test comparing the field (likely encoding or a field representative of encoding) fails when the encoding is not passed on. The bug report confirms this by listing which input streams are affected.

The recent bug reports retrieved are unrelated to this encoding passing issue.

This diagnosis aligns with the test failure and issue description.

Next, it is appropriate to fix `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream` to ensure all relevant archive input streams receive the encoding parameter if it was set on the factory.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
